einzeiler: Analyzing the Buffalo Bills offensive and defensive line depth for the upcoming season.
kurzfassung: Joe Marino and Jerry Ostroski launch a new weekly series breaking down the Buffalo Bills' trench units. They evaluate the starting offensive tackle tandem, guard depth, and the key pieces along the defensive line. The hosts also discuss scheme fits under Jim Leonard and how the team's extensive backup experience will impact the season.
stichpunkte: Dion Dawkins and Spencer Brown anchor the offensive line, with discussion on Dawkins's weight management and Brown's durability.
Offensive line depth includes recent additions and developmental pieces like Tylen Grable and the practice squad signing.
Alec Anderson steps in as the starting left guard, drawing comparisons to previous first-year starters.
Dion Walker enters the season with high expectations and is expected to thrive in a gap control defensive scheme.
The defensive tackle rotation features a battle for snaps among Greg Gaines, Dwayne Carter, and returning players.
T.J. Parker displays sound technique and high upside as a rookie pass rusher in the defensive front.
Greg Rousseau and an expanded outside linebacker group offer versatility and depth in Jim Leonard's defense.
beschreibung:
Buffalo Bills' trench warfare takes center stage as Joe Marino and Jerry Ostroski break down the O-line and D-line dynamics shaping the team's 2024 outlook. Can Dion Dawkins' revamped physique and Spencer Brown's health provide the stability Buffalo needs up front? With Alec Anderson stepping in at left guard, the pressure is on for the new-look offensive line.
On defense, Deone Walker’s upside as a gap-control specialist draws major buzz, while Jim Leonhard’s scheme raises questions about how TJ Sanders, Landon Jackson, and Ed Oliver will rotate. The episode also spotlights outside linebackers Greg Rousseau, TJ Parker, and Michael Hoecht in a crowded edge group. Are the Bills equipped to neutralize star pass rushers like Will Anderson and Myles Garrett—and can their own front set the tone for a playoff run?
